title: Device CSV exports: inventory, service status and disable reasons

prose.text: The portal and the API both export device data as CSV. The three API exports are limited to 3 calls a day, so a filter that silently fails costs a call: [[zcc.api.rate-limits:hourly-and-daily-limits]]. Whether that allowance is per endpoint or shared is open: [[zcc.api.rate-limits:download-cap-scope]].

prose.label: Allowance.
prose.text: The three download endpoints are limited to 3 calls a day: [[zcc.api.rate-limits:hourly-and-daily-limits]].

prose.label: Disable reasons.
prose.text: Users give reasons only when the app profile asks for them: [[zcc.app-profiles.advanced-settings:send-disable-reason]]. {{disable-reasons-call}} {{python-disable-reasons-header}}

console-exports.statement: The Device Management page exports device details (all fields or chosen fields), disable reasons (up to the five most recent times each service was disabled), service status (Internet & SaaS, Private Access and ZDX as On, Off or Error) and partner login details.

quotes: Device Details (All Fields): Includes fields such as manufacturer, model, username, machine hostname, UDID, etc.
Disable Reasons: Displays the reasons a service was disabled up to the 5 most recent times the service was disabled.
Service Status: The status of Internet & SaaS, Private Access, and Digital Experience (ZDX). Can be in an On, Off, or Error state.
Partner Login Details: Includes partner device fields such as UDID, Platform, Device ID, login name, and cloud.

download-filters.statement: The device and service-status downloads filter by `osTypes` and `registrationTypes`, each a comma-separated list of codes; a null `osTypes` means all OS types.

expect.description:
Filter the list of devices by operating systems. The default value is null, which represents ALL OS types. The following values represent different OS types:

  • 1 - iOS
  • 2 - Android
  • 3 - Windows
  • 4 - macOS
  • 5 - Linux

A sample API call: https://api-mobile.zscalerbeta.net/papi/public/v1/downloadDevices?osTypes=1,2

Filter the list of devices by registration types or states. The following values represent different device states:

  • 0 - All states except Removed
  • 1 - Registered
  • 3 - Removal pending
  • 4 - Unregistered
  • 5 - Removed
  • 6 - Quarantined

A sample API call: https://api-mobile.zscalerbeta.net/papi/public/v1/downloadDevices?registrationTypes=1,3

disable-reasons-call.statement: The disable-reasons download requires `startDate`, takes an optional `endDate` and `osTypes`, and takes the time zone as a `Time-Zone` request header rather than a query parameter.

python-disable-reasons-header.statement: The Python `download_disable_reasons` moves a `time_zone` argument into the `Time-Zone` header and sends the reformatted `startDate` and `endDate` as query parameters.

evidence.after: def download_disable_reasons(self, query_params=None, filename: str = None):

python-keyword-filters-dropped.statement: Called with `query_params=` as a keyword, the Python `download_devices` and `download_service_status` send no OS or registration filter: the decorator replaces `os_types` and `registration_types` in that dict with `osTypes` and `registrationTypes`, and the method then builds its request parameters only from `os_types` and `registration_types`. Passed positionally, the dict skips the decorator's mapping and the method translates it itself.

python-all-rejected.statement: The Python SDK maps registration type `all` to 0 and then keeps only truthy codes, so `all` is dropped: alone it raises an invalid registration type error, and alongside other types it is silently left out.
